sentences: Constant-delay enumeration aims to produce query answers promptly after an initial preprocessing phase.
The source asks for unconditional lower bounds for natural queries, including a distance-two example.
The target is to prove an inherent limitation directly rather than obtain it only from an unproved fine-grained conjecture.
Such a result would strengthen the foundations of query-enumeration classifications and clarify which costs are mathematically unavoidable.

The source's preprocessing budget, RAM operations, and precise distance-two output convention matter, because lower bounds can change when stronger indexing or different output requirements are permitted.
